title: WL-MT408-SealArchiveRetentionAndPortableRestore
clause: Seal, archive, retain, restore and remove WP-local working databases as non-authoritative project-qualified artifacts without weakening canonical SurrealDB truth or project portability.

conditional_execution.approved: Execute this contract normally after MT-407.
conditional_execution.rejected: Do not edit product code or create local archive artifacts; record validator-checked NOT_APPLICABLE_BY_MT401_REJECTION.

scope.summary: GOAL: Define the end-of-WP lifecycle for a conditional WpLocalStore. Closing or archiving a WP first drains or classifies every promotion intent, independently records the current canonical SurrealDB/EventLedger watermark, closes the single broker handle, checkpoints, seals the database and writes a content-addressed project-relative manifest. Restore validates identity, hash, schema, key reference and canonical watermark before opening read-only or rebuilding disposable state. Retention cleanup is bounded, recoverable and incapable of deleting or changing canonical data.
forbidden_paths: Archiving or restoring a WP-local database as canonical Handshake state
Absolute machine paths, plaintext keys, credentials or content samples in manifests
Reopening a sealed database for ordinary mutation without a governed lifecycle transition
Deleting canonical SurrealDB records, EventLedger events, Notes, Loom, CKC, Tailor, Studio or Locus data during local retention cleanup
Copying an archive across project/WP scope without identity and authorization verification
acceptance_criteria: WP close refuses to seal while an intent is RUNNING or ambiguous; each remaining intent is independently classified as canonically promoted, stale, rejected or explicitly local-only before broker shutdown.

Seal performs a bounded checkpoint, closes the single broker, makes the local database immutable and emits a manifest containing format/schema versions, project_id, wp_id, content hash, byte size, key reference ID, canonical watermark, intent counts and relative locator, with no secret or absolute path.
Archive storage is content-addressed and project-relative; moving the entire project to another folder or disk preserves discovery and validation without rewriting embedded absolute paths.

Restore verifies archive hash, embedded project/WP identity, schema compatibility, current authorization and a fresh canonical SurrealDB/EventLedger watermark before any open; mismatch fails closed to quarantine or allowlist rebuild.

A valid restored archive opens read-only for inspection by default and can resume mutable use only through an explicit governed transition that reconciles all intents against current canonical revisions.

Retention cleanup uses a typed preview and recoverable quarantine/trash phase before irreversible removal, targets only exact closed WP-local artifacts and cannot reach project roots or canonical storage.
Archive and restore never introduce Notes/Loom/CKC/Tailor/Studio or canonical Locus content, and never describe local rows as the recovery source of truth.
proof_targets: Close a WP with pending, promoted, stale and ambiguous intents and prove only fully classified state can be sealed.
Inspect a sealed manifest and prove stable hash/schema/watermark metadata with no secret, content sample or absolute path.
Move the project tree to a different root and restore the exact project/WP archive through relative discovery.
Tamper with archive bytes, identity, schema and canonical watermark independently and prove fail-closed quarantine or rebuild.
Preview and execute retention cleanup against fixtures adjacent to canonical/project files and prove only exact eligible local artifacts enter recoverable removal.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: The archive state machine is backend-owned. MT-409 supplies the operator and Argus surfaces for seal, restore and retention status/actions.

target_entries: WP-local working store > Closing and sealing a WP
WP-local working store > Archive, restore and project moves
WP-local working store > Retention cleanup and recovery

same_project_private_resource_cases: Possession of a same-project archive grants no access beyond the current project/WP ResourceGrant.
cross_account_negative_cases: An archive copied across project/account scope fails identity, authorization and key-reference validation without existence disclosure.
derived_resource_non_widening_cases: Archive copy, project movement, restore and retention preserve the original AccessSpace and source-scope intersection.
revocation_and_context_switch_cases: Revocation or context switch during seal/restore/retention cancels the action and invalidates active handles.
remote_saas_mcp_sync_cases: Archive and restore are local/project-relative and expose no Turso Cloud, SaaS, MCP or replica synchronization.
metadata_side_channel_cases: Manifests and diagnostics expose only authorized redacted IDs, hashes, counts, versions and key references, never content, credentials, keys or absolute paths.

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.reason: Seal, restore, quarantine and retention lifecycle transitions produce attributable derived events with canonical watermark references.
Manifest validation, broker closure, archive integrity and canonical mismatch need structured redacted diagnostics.
Checkpoint, hash, copy, restore and retention jobs expose progress, cancellation, exact target and terminal result.

risk_if_missed: A stale or relocated archive can reopen as mutable truth, leak secrets or absolute paths, cross project boundaries, or let broad cleanup remove unrelated project or canonical data.

risks: An archive is copied into a different project and accepted by filename alone.
A sealed database is reopened for writes after canonical state advances.
A manifest leaks an encryption key or machine-specific project path.
Retention cleanup follows a broad or unresolved path and removes unrelated files.
minimum_controls: Embedded identity, content hash, key-reference and fresh canonical watermark validation.
Read-only restore default plus explicit reconciliation before mutable use.
Exact resolved-target preview and recoverable removal phase.
